To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a new finite element model for the human lung, including interlobar septae and the heart cavity, that can be used in the study of lung mechanics.
the finite element method is a powerful tool to study the mechanics and the fluid mechanics of the lungs.
the finite element model of lungs including inter-lobar fissures can be used to study the effect of fissures and the effect of the heart cavity on lung mechanics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a three-dimensional, finite element method to model the mechanical behavior of the lung.
the finite element modeling of the lung and its interactions with the heart.
the development of a finite element model of the human lung that can be used to simulate lung motion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present finite element model of the lungs and the heart cavity can be used for the prediction of the pressure distribution and the stress state of the lungs during respiration, and the pressure distribution in the heart cavity during cardiac filling.

the finite element method, when applied to the modeling of lung mechanics, is capable of providing a realistic description of lung mechanics, and that it is a powerful tool in studying lung mechanics.

a finite element model of the human lung has been constructed, which is based on an anatomically correct geometry and which incorporates the effects of tissue anisotropy, inhomogeneity, nonlinearity and the interaction with the thorax and the heart cavity, as well as the effect of gravity.

the present work provides an efficient and accurate method to model lung deformation and its interaction with the surrounding heart cavity, including the effects of interlobar fissure.
we have successfully developed a finite element model for the human lungs including the heart cavity, and the interlobar fissure.
a finite element method for simulating the mechanical response of a lung model including the heart cavity and interlobar fissure has been presented.

we can use the finite element method to solve the equations of motion for a deformable solid.
